title: Rice and Peas
subtitle: Jamaican rice cooked in coconut milk with pigeon peas and scotch bonnet
excerpt: The essential Jamaican Sunday side dish and the traditional partner to jerk chicken: long-grain rice cooked in coconut milk with pigeon peas, a whole scotch bonnet, spring onions, and thyme. Rich and fragrant without being spicy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rice and peas is the cornerstone of Jamaican Sunday cooking and the standard accompaniment to jerk chicken. Despite the name, the peas are traditionally pigeon peas (gungo peas) or kidney beans — not the green peas that the name might suggest to British ears. Pigeon peas are the authentic Sunday choice; kidney beans are the more common weekday substitute. The scotch bonnet is cooked whole and unbroken, which gives the rice a warm, fruity flavour without making it hot; it must not be pierced or the dish becomes fiery. Coconut milk replaces part of the water to give the rice a rich, slightly sweet quality. The dish is cooked by the absorption method: the rice soaks up all the liquid and the result is fluffy, flavoured grains.

recipeTools.notes: A saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.

content.text: The scotch bonnet must stay whole and unbroken throughout cooking; it flavours the rice without making it hot. Remove it carefully before serving. Do not lift the lid during the final 15 minutes of cooking or the steam will escape and the rice will not cook evenly. Once the rice has absorbed all the liquid, remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes to steam finish.

items.preparation: rinsed under cold water until the water runs clear

content.text: Pour the coconut milk into a large saucepan and add enough water to make 700 ml of liquid total. Add the pigeon peas, scotch bonnet (whole), spring onions, garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to the boil.
Add the rinsed rice, stir once, and bring back to the boil. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook for 18 to 20 minutes until the rice has absorbed all the liquid.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. Remove the scotch bonnet, spring onions, garlic, and thyme sprigs. Fluff with a fork and serve.
